title: 2024 budget: paramedics, speed cameras, transit
subtitle: Child care funding, MobilityPLUS, youth fund referred to staff, and a food bank grant motion withdrawn
overview: The Strategic Planning and Budget Committee reviewed the equitable services and opportunities part of the draft 2024 Region of Waterloo budget. It recommended six service expansions or budget changes for Council's final budget vote on December 13: child care under the Canada-wide plan, two paramedic services items, automated speed enforcement, and two MobilityPLUS changes.

The speed enforcement expansion drew the most debate, with a recommendation to add cameras and staff to process tickets {{vote:m6}}. Staff said the program is expected to pay for itself, with any net revenue going into a road safety reserve. Councillors also heard a preview of proposed GRT fare changes, which need no motion until budget day.

A proposed $500,000 annual youth fund was not adopted. The committee instead asked staff to report on how the money would be allocated and where it would come from {{vote:m11}}. Because these are committee recommendations, Council can still change any of them. A councillor withdrew a proposed food bank grant increase and said it will return on final budget day.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended adding positions for the Canada-wide Early Learning and Child Care plan to the 2024 operating budget, which staff said are fully funded by federal and provincial money.
The committee recommended including the 2024 implementation of the Paramedic Services Master Plan in the operating budget.
The committee recommended a community paramedicine expansion, which staff said is fully provincially funded.
The committee recommended expanding automated speed enforcement in the 2024 operating budget, including the staffing described in Appendix A {{vote:m6}}.
The committee recommended adding $300,000 from the MobilityPLUS Rural Reserve to the 2024 budget, reducing the 2024 rural levy for MobilityPLUS services.
The committee recommended a service expansion for Urban MobilityPLUS in the 2024 operating budget.
The committee referred the proposed $500,000 youth fund to staff to report on allocation, eligibility and funding sources by December 13, 2023.

debate: On speed cameras, one councillor asked whether staffing could start smaller and grow as needed. Staff replied that processing staff scale with the number of cameras, so fewer staff would mean fewer cameras in 2024. Staff also said the multi-year plan reflected earlier Council direction to move faster.

Other councillors backed the expansion as a response to road safety concerns raised for months, especially speeding on regional roads through towns. One councillor opposed it, citing the cost, fines that hit lower-income drivers harder, and tickets issued when schools are empty. That councillor suggested time-of-day limits and portable cameras. Staff said a report on time limits was coming the following week.

On MobilityPLUS, councillors questioned the use of a rural reserve meant for vehicle replacement. Staff said the draw is temporary and phased out over several years. A rural councillor also asked how trips are counted and why the township levy is high relative to use. Staff agreed to bring back clearer data on unaccommodated trips.

On the youth fund, supporters pointed to gaps in youth mental health and belonging. Others worried the purpose was too broad and that funding it from reserves would leave a gap in later years. Several asked for staff advice on priorities and funding, while the mover said the supporting data already existed.

On fares, councillors raised concerns about a higher cash fare and a possible single-fare increase. They asked about a longer transfer window, youth eligibility for the affordable transit program, and free travel for support persons. Staff agreed to look into these.
